thread.title: UPDATE 1-BlackBerry quarterly results beat on software strength

title: UPDATE 1-BlackBerry quarterly results beat on software strength
text:
June 22, 2018 / 11:16 AM / in 4 minutes BlackBerry signals slowing sales on subscription switch Laharee Chatterjee 4 Min Read
(Reuters) - Canada’s BlackBerry Ltd ( BB.TO ) signaled slowing sales in its software and services business as it switches to a subscription-based model, sending its shares down nearly 10 percent. The new BlackBerry Key2 smartphone is seen at a product launch event for the device in Manhattan in New York, U.S., June 7, 2018. REUTERS/Mike Segar
The company forecast 8 percent to 10 percent growth for the business in 2019, compared with 20 percent in 2018, overshadowing its first-quarter revenue and profit beat.
BlackBerry will no longer be selling its software and services on a licensing basis and will have to convince companies to agree to subscriptions, Chief Executive Officer John Chen said on a post-earnings call.
The growth guidance is lower than what the market has been expecting, and that’s mainly due to the company having to recognize enterprise software revenue based on subscription, Morningstar analyst Ali Mogharabi said.
A number of software companies, including Oracle Corp ( ORCL.N ) and Adobe Systems Inc ( ADBE.O ), are moving much of their services to the cloud and relying on subscriptions for a steady stream of revenue.
“Our long-term goal is 90 percent-plus in recurring software and services revenue, which I believe we can accomplish within a year,” Chen said.
BlackBerry, which dominated the smartphone market nearly a decade ago before losing out to Apple Inc’s ( AAPL.O ) iPhones and Android devices, has been trying to win investor confidence and make money by selling software to manage mobile devices to corporations and government agencies.
As part of the transition, the company is also focusing on making software for next-generation driverless cars based on its QNX platform.
CFRA Research Angelo Zino said the turnaround is working for BlackBerry and investors need to keep a long-term view on the company.
“You don’t see big top-line and bottom-line growth because the company is still adjusting every quarter from the winding of their hardware business,” Zino said.
China’s Baidu Inc ( BIDU.O ) already uses QNX in the operating system of its autonomous driving project, Apollo. BlackBerry has also partnered with Tata Motors Ltd’s ( TAMO.NS ) Jaguar, Ford Motor Co ( F.N ) and auto technology companies Denso and Aptiv Plc ( APTV.N ).
U.S.-listed shares of BlackBerry slumped 9.8 percent to $10.54 in morning trading.
For the first quarter, the company’s net loss was $60 million, or 11 cents per share, compared with a profit of $671 million, or $1.23 per share, a year earlier.
The comparable quarter reflected a one-time arbitration payment of $940 million from Qualcomm Inc ( QCOM.O ).
Excluding items, the company earned 3 cents per share. Analysts were expecting the company to break even on a per-share basis, according to Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S.
Total revenue fell 9.4 percent to $213 million, but still beat analysts’ estimate of $208 million. Reporting by Laharee Chatterjee in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva
